turn.text:
During weekday business hours (09:00–17:59), traffic from the R&D group (10.1.5.0/24) to the WeChat and video-streaming destinations is now dropped. Outside those hours it is allowed. I haven't tested it with traffic, only read the rules back from the live ruleset and checked `/etc/nftables.conf` with `nft -c`.

- **WeChat:** 198.51.100.21 on tcp 80 and 443.
- **Video streaming:** 198.51.100.20 on tcp 80, 443 and 1935.
- **Rule placement:** the two drop rules sit at the top of `inet filter forward`, ahead of the existing accepts. They carry the comments `rd-block-wechat` and `rd-block-video`.
- **Time window:** it uses `meta day` (Monday–Friday) and `meta hour` (09:00–17:59). The device clock is UTC, so the window follows UTC. If R&D works in another timezone, the hours need shifting.
- **Persistence:** I added the same two rules to `/etc/nftables.conf`, so they survive a reload. The original is saved as `/etc/nftables.conf.bak`.

There are two things you may want to look at:

- **Config drift:** the live ruleset has extra rules that `/etc/nftables.conf` lacks. These are the accept for 10.1.5.0/24 and its SNAT rule. If the firewall reloads from the file, those rules will be lost. I didn't change that.
- **Interface mismatch:** the site notes say R&D sits behind eth1, but eth1 is 192.168.10.1/24 and 10.1.0.1/16 is on eth4. My rules match on source IP only, so they work either way.
